measurementsTaken.name: byte-identity at neutral importance (the safety gate, FORGET-01, claim 1)
measurementsTaken.result: PASS — a NEUTRAL/legacy memory (no memoryType, no proof/usefulness enrichment) at EVENT-AGE 0 scores + ranks IDENTICALLY three ways: forget OFF, forget ON-at-neutral (with a live forgetAlpha=1.0), and a pre-forget reference (the forget field absent). scoreForgetOff=1, scoreForgetOnNeutral=1, scoreForgetAbsent=1; rankForgetOff=1, rankForgetOnNeutral=1, rankForgetAbsent=1; byteIdentical=true. At Δt=0 the FadeMem factor is 0.5 + 0.5·exp(0) = 1.0 EXACTLY for ANY λ/β/imp, so a fresh neutral row is never reordered even with the decay enabled at a live alpha. This is the LOCKED safety property: the decay never silently shifts a legacy/neutral row.

measurementsTaken.name: the deterministic decay effect (FORGET-01, claim 2)
measurementsTaken.result: MEASURED — an OLD (90-day event-age) low-importance EPHEMERAL memory (memoryType:"episodic", β=1.2) decays BELOW a FRESH (1-day) DURABLE memory (memoryType:"semantic", β=0.8) under the fixed BENCH_NOW fake clock. Recovered as the per-memory forget CONTRIBUTION (the on/off boosted-score ratio, since forget is a pure multiplicand and every other alpha is 0): oldEphemeralForgetFactor=0.5534545198841266, freshDurableForgetFactor=0.9945726783223208, forgetFactorGap=0.44111815843819413, decayedBelow=true. This is the INTENDED FadeMem behavior, MEASURED — the per-type β + the event-age both push the old-ephemeral's factor lower. It is NOT a 'decay improves QA' accuracy claim (FadeMem's decay is never ablated in isolation — see honestyProtocol + deferredToOperator). The factor only ever demotes (∈ (0,1]); the decay RANKS, never GATES (no result is dropped).

measurementsTaken.name: footprint unchanged when the eviction scaffold is off/dormant (FORGET-02, claim 3)
measurementsTaken.result: PASS — seeding 5 real rows on the SqliteMemoryAdapter (incl. a deliberately stale ~10-year-dormant low-importance ephemeral row, an eviction CANDIDATE a live policy would touch) and running the WIRED SCAFFOLD-DORMANT runLifecycleSweep (createSqliteMemoryLifecycleStore over the same getDb() handle — the 112-04 daemon-cron path) evicts/demotes NOTHING: rowCountBefore=5, rowCountAfter=5, evictedMarkerCount=0, demotedMarkerCount=0, and the sweep report is {scanned:5, promoted:0, demoted:0, evicted:0}; footprintUnchanged=true. The sweep is wired + live (it scanned the candidates) but its demote/evict step is dead by construction (LIVE_EVICTION=false as const) — the footprint is unchanged. This is the sole footprint claim: the dormant scaffold evicts nothing. The synthetic FadeMem storage-reduction headline (object-counts on a synthetic benchmark, not bytes) is NOT measured here and NOT echoed.

measurementsTaken.name: zero category regression (FORGET-01, claim 4)
measurementsTaken.result: PASS — the recall hot path with forget OFF is byte-identical to a no-forget baseline run (the forget field absent) on the same mixed-age, mixed-type fixtures (every memoryType + a range of event-ages): baselineOrderLength=4, forgetOffOrderLength=4, noRegression=true. The shipping default (forget off) moves no stable-category ranking; the Phase-106 baseline holds byte-for-byte when forget is off.

deferredToOperator.name: the costed QA-accuracy impact of the FadeMem decay (a question-answering accuracy delta of the decay-on vs decay-off ranker over real answers)
deferredToOperator.why: The keyless bench MEASURES the decay's deterministic MECHANICAL effect (an old low-importance ephemeral memory's forget factor decays below a fresh durable one) + byte-identity + footprint-unchanged + no-regression — all at $0. A QA-accuracy comparison of the decay-on vs decay-off ranker is a DIFFERENT measurement: it needs a real answer model + a real LLM judge (cross-judge ≥2 per the credibility protocol) to score answers, plus a costed run, all of which costs real spend + keys. Crucially, FadeMem's decay is never ablated in isolation in the source work (its standalone forgetting-curve evidence is weak — its fusion component dominates its ablations), so there is NO keyless evidence for a 'decay improves QA' claim and a fresh accuracy number here would be fabricated. Kept STRICTLY SEPARATE from the keyless mechanical claims above.
